text:
T.J. Hughes went undrafted, scored 57 points in 40 games for Michigan last season, and signed with Colorado as a free agent. Nineteen games into his NHL career he is playing 15 minutes a night for one of the league's best teams, which tells you the coaches like what they see.

The scoring hasn't followed. Two goals in 19 games and none in his last ten, on 3.8 expected goals over that stretch. For the season he has 5.78 individual expected goals and 45 shots, so the volume and quality are there; the 4.4% shooting rate is not something that usually lasts. Our numbers flag him as due.

The concern is defensive. The Avalanche have just 46% of expected goals with him on the ice at 5v5, eight points worse than without him, even though they win the shot attempts (51%). The Hockey Writers argued he has more to offer than the numbers show, and five assists in ten games back that up a little.

As a rookie, his range is wide. Watch whether the minutes hold while he waits for the puck to go in.
headline: T.J. Hughes is due a goal
